capabilities.title: Hosted-runner cause measured, not listed
capabilities.requirement: The reason the WebView2 remote-debugging endpoint never appears on the hosted image is established by a probing pass with named one-line probes, whose reading is recorded whatever it says.
capabilities.observed_gap: On the hosted runner the app boots (EBWebView present, three webview children, the staged UI log showing four command calls within one second) yet DevToolsActivePort is never seen within 90s. Identical across CI runs 34162118841, 34251573399, 34256490781, 34280136892 and 34365300658, and identical under runtime 151 and 152, which falsifies the runtime-major hypothesis. Three candidates remain UNMEASURED and none has been probed on the runner: the WebView2/Edge policy state on the image, the module version the host processes actually loaded, and any session or service-account property of the runner.

verification.acceptance:
`conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-09-11-hosted-runner-endpoint-cause-closed/evidence/reading.md` records, for each of the three named probes — policy state, loaded module versions, and session identity — what the hosted `windows-2025` runner returned on a named CI run, identifying the job and its steps BY NAME and stating the run by id, event, branch and conclusion. The policy-state and session-identity readings are carried forward from `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-09-11-hosted-runner-endpoint-cause-probed/evidence/reading.md`, cited rather than re-measured. The LOADED MODULE VERSIONS reading is taken while its subject processes are ALIVE — the probe's module section invoked inside the `WebView2 session isolation (diagnostic)` step's bare-app window, above the teardown that previously ran 0.645 s ahead of it — proven by the committed gate `grep -c "\[diag\] (2) msedgewebview2 : [1-9]"` over the captured job log reading `1`, not asserted. Each hosted-runner reading is stated BESIDE its dev-host control value, captured by the same `scripts/webview2-cause-probe.ps1` rather than hand-approximated, so each pair discriminates a hosted-image property from a universal one.

The ELEVATION difference the probing pass named but never varied is VARIED, with a control on both sides: the same script's capture from an elevated dev-host shell (carrying its own `IsElevatedAdmin: True` line, so elevation is machine-proven rather than operator-attested) and the routine arm re-run in that same elevated session under `CONDUCTOR_A11Y_STRICT=1`, graded on its printed verdict, stated beside the committed non-elevated control (12 passing / 2 skipped, banner `[webview2 152.0.4191.66 windows]`, 2026-09-10). The elevated result is bounded to the host it was measured on; a null result retires elevation as measured on THIS host and never as a universal retirement.

On that evidence the reading states the decision the four readings support — whether the endpoint failure is remediable or permanent — and names the mechanism it rests on. Where the readings do NOT support that decision, the reading says so explicitly and names the candidate set that remains, and this capability is not claimed on the strength of the wording.

A probe that returned nothing — an absent registry key, no live process, or an Access Denied on module enumeration — is recorded as having returned that rather than omitted, and a reading that contradicts the expected cause is recorded unchanged; the untouched `WebView2 cause probes (diagnostic)` step's continuing `no live process` line for its own module section is recorded as expected rather than suppressed. The reading carries no absolute host path, proven by the committed `grep -cE` hygiene gate over `reading.md` reading `0`, not asserted. The run's red is attributed to the standing WebView2 session-creation failure rather than to this chunk, and no green, conformance or platform-capability claim is drawn from any probe.
verification.ref: conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-09-11-hosted-runner-endpoint-cause-closed/evidence/reading.md — cause ESTABLISHED by variation with a control on both sides. Arm A: module reading taken inside the isolation step's live window, CI runs 34645345201 + 34654076633, proven by `grep -c "\[diag\] (2) msedgewebview2 : [1-9]"` = 1. Arm C: driver/runtime major skew varied and RETIRED (install SKIPPED, `majors: 2 1`, modules 152.0.4191.66 vs 153.0.4234.32 prior, every isolation reading byte-identical across both runs). capabilities.notes:
2026-09-11 (2026-09-11-hosted-runner-endpoint-cause-probed, wrap P7.3): UN-CLAIMED — not refined. The chunk drove three named probes on the hosted `windows-2025` runner at CI run `34586959536` and recorded every reading; what it could not do is reach the acceptance's second half, that the readings are together sufficient to DECIDE whether the endpoint failure is remediable or permanent. The acceptance is not what overreached: that clause is what makes this capability worth holding, so it stands unedited and the capability returns to the pool at its current status. The follow-up entry `Hosted-runner endpoint cause closed` (Epoch 1, minted this wrap) claims it when the measurement is whole.

What the chunk DID establish, which is committed evidence at `conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-09-11-hosted-runner-endpoint-cause-probed/evidence/reading.md`:

TWO candidates RETIRED. (1) Policy state — all five probed Edge / EdgeUpdate / EdgeWebView keys, machine and user hives, ABSENT on the hosted runner AND ABSENT on the dev host, so no policy difference exists that could explain a behavioural one. (2) Session context — session-0 and non-interactive are both falsified: the runner is `SessionId 2` with `UserInteractive: True`, corroborated independently by the isolation step's own `tasklist` showing the app and its webview children on Console session 2.

ONE new lead NAMED and UNVARIED. The runner runs elevated (`IsElevatedAdmin: True`) where the dev host does not (`False`), both readings captured by the same `scripts/webview2-cause-probe.ps1` rather than one being hand-approximated. This is a difference, not a demonstrated cause — no probe varied it, and nothing measured says de-elevating opens the endpoint.

ONE probe RETURNED NOTHING, for a MEASURED cause rather than an unknown one. The loaded-module-version probe found no live process because of WHERE its step sits: the preceding `WebView2 session isolation (diagnostic)` step stops the app it started, and its last lines are stamped `10:14:58.9039327Z` / `10:14:58.9049097Z` / `10:14:58.9060743Z` / `10:14:58.9421153Z` against the cause-probe's completion marker at `10:14:59.5867824Z` — **0.645 s later**. The same isolation step's `tasklist` at `10:13:21.76Z` shows `conductor-tauri.exe` and three `msedgewebview2.exe` alive during it. The probe is correct; its position is what made the reading unreachable.

capabilities.notes:
2026-09-11 (route Phase 4, operator): TWO planning obligations folded into this capability rather than minted as chunks of their own.

(1) WebView2 runtime pin disposition. The CI-fetched Evergreen bootstrapper floats always-latest with ONE stated exit condition in security-plan's third dependency class: the a11y job actually gating. This capability's terminal fork IS that exit condition, so whichever way the terminal lands, the float is dispositioned in the same chunk (pinned if the job gates, retired if the CI half is excluded). Surfaced by the security validator during the route run; folded on operator direction.

(2) Landmark coupling to an unbuilt surface. The console footer contentinfo strip is designed but not shipped, and a11y-plan bans a landmark-less window. If the routine arm starts gating, that ban could turn the unshipped footer into a RED inside the very gate this capability is trying to make green. This is an INDEPENDENT second cause of red, living in a surface 0.3.0 deliberately does not build, so it cannot be reasoned about from the endpoint question alone. Planning for this capability must MEASURE whether the routine specs pass against the console as it stands before promising a green terminal; a promise made without that measurement is the failure this note predicts. Operator-supplied at the Phase 4 review.

2026-09-16 (2026-09-16-a11y-ci-gate-at-an-honest-terminal, phase P5): acceptance PREMISE-CHECKED and carried forward unchanged, not concretized. Two reasons, both recorded at the never-weaken checkpoint. (a) It is already concrete — it names the printed verdict, the pass/skip counts and the expected set — and research confirmed the shipped mechanism implements exactly that: `Assert-A11yVerdict` asserts the driven-session banner, the `Spec Files:` failed count and a skip tally against an expected set of two, so the premise the acceptance rests on holds at HEAD. (b) Concretizing it into this chunk's chosen remedy (a limited-token launch of the wdio leg) would place every clause DOWNSTREAM of an unmeasured premise — whether de-elevation produces the DevToolsActivePort endpoint is precisely what this chunk measures — which is weaker than the outcome it would replace. Both arms of the acceptance stay reachable: a green routine arm, or a ratified permanent exclusion whose basis is the measured cause (elevation, established by direct variation with a control on both sides and confirmed a third time in run 35079315258) and which names its owner.

2026-09-16 (2026-09-16-medium-integrity-launch-for-the-a11y-routine-arm, phase P5): acceptance PREMISE-CHECKED and carried forward unchanged for the second consecutive chunk, not concretized — and the reason has MOVED, so it is recorded rather than inherited.

(a) Already concrete, and its premise re-verified at HEAD this phase: `Assert-A11yVerdict` (`scripts/agent-run.ps1:68-100`) asserts the `^[webview2 [^\]]*windows` driven-session banner, the last `Spec Files:` line's failed count, and a skip tally against `$A11yExpectedSkips = 2` (`:62`) — exactly the printed verdict, counts and expected set the acceptance names. The `.sh` twin carries the same semantics at `:188`/`:202`/`:225`.

(b) The predecessor declined to concretize because whether de-elevation produces the endpoint was the thing it was measuring. That premise is now MEASURED on the dev host (integrity label, not the administrator role, is the discriminator — three legs, control on both sides). What remains unmeasured is narrower and different: whether that finding TRANSFERS to the runner, whose session context differs. Concretizing into this chunk's chosen remedy (a `CreateRestrictedToken` + `SetTokenInformation` + `CreateProcessAsUser` launch) would place every clause downstream of that still-open transfer premise, which is weaker than the outcome it would replace.

Measured this phase and recorded so the next planner need not re-derive it: matrix obligation 2's feared second cause of red — the designed-but-unshipped console `contentinfo` footer — CANNOT fire in the routine arm. The arm runs `accessibility.e2e.ts` alone (`wdio.conf.ts:320`); that file carries no landmark assertion across its 14 `it()` blocks; axe runs `withTags(['wcag2a','wcag2aa','wcag21aa'])` and every landmark-family rule in the installed axe-core 4.12.0 (`region`, `landmark-one-main`, `landmark-unique`, `landmark-complementary-is-top-level`, `landmark-banner-is-top-level`, `landmark-contentinfo-is-top-level`, `landmark-no-duplicate-contentinfo`) is tagged `best-practice`, so none of the 68 selected rules is one of them; and the only three `contentinfo` mentions in the test tree are SR-arm records of its ABSENCE as a finding. The DOM gap is real (`contentinfo` and `<footer` both 0 hits in `crates/conductor-tauri/ui/src/`) — a11y-plan §11's landmark-less-window ban simply has no automated enforcement in this arm. Obligation 1 (the Evergreen pin disposition) stands unchanged and is owed whichever arm the terminal lands on.

Both acceptance arms remain reachable. The measurement that decides which is the operator-authorized ci-probe named in the plan's Test Commands; the CI read deliberately asserts only exit 0, because asserting success would forecast the outcome this chunk exists to measure.

2026-09-17 (2026-09-16-medium-integrity-launch-for-the-a11y-routine-arm, wrap P7.3): un-claimed, and the EXCLUSION ARM IS NOW DEAD ON MEASUREMENT.

The acceptance stands unchanged and was deliberately NOT refined downward — it is correct as written, and the world is one small fix from meeting it.

Arm 1 (green printed verdict) is not met, but for the first time it is REACHABLE and nearly reached. Run 35192876641 — hosted `windows-2022`, native WebView2 runtime 131.0.2903.86, msedgedriver pinned to 131.0.2903.86, HIGH integrity, no launcher — created the first hosted-runner WebView2 session in this project's history (`DevToolsActivePort` in 1 s, banner `[webview2 131.0.2903.86 windows]`) and ran the routine arm at 11 passing / 1 failing / 2 skipped, the two skips being the expected live-hold set. SC 2.4.3 (`:397`) PASSES on runtime 131.

Arm 2 (ratified permanent exclusion) is now FORECLOSED. The endpoint demonstrably opens on a hosted runner, so a permanent exclusion would have been ratified on a false basis. Recorded here so no future chunk re-opens it: it had a measured basis for roughly one day (the driver-alone isolation at Medium, runs 35145664132 / 35147042449 / 35150449243) and that basis was superseded twice — first by the transport comparison, then by the coherent-pair run. Holding the terminal open was vindicated on both occasions.

The single red is `:384` (SC 2.1.1) and it is a COUNTING-BASIS defect in the assertion, not an accessibility defect: expected and received bracket lists are identical to the character — same six controls, same order, same one wrap of the focus cycle — and only the prefix differs, expected "6 reached" against received "12 reached". The expectation counts DISTINCT controls; the label counts VISITS. Record it as "12 visits / 6 distinct", never as a bare count. The reachability property SC 2.1.1 asserts is satisfied, and the proof is inside the failure message.

Not established: why the focus cycle wraps on the runner and did not on the dev host at runtime 152 (the 2026-09-10 green). The assertion is environment-sensitive and the first successful CI run of this arm is what exposed it.

Owner: the successor entry minted at this wrap's P5, `conductor-0.3.0/working-route.md:37`, which carries the working configuration, the failure's own evidence, and the four unresolved operator escalations.

2026-09-17 (2026-09-17-a11y-routine-arm-terminal-on-the-measured-configuration, phase P5): acceptance CONCRETIZED for the first time in this capability's life — the dead arm struck, arm 1 kept verbatim. Two predecessors premise-checked and carried it forward unchanged; this chunk narrows it, which strengthens rather than weakens.

Arm 2 (a ratified permanent exclusion) is REMOVED. It was recorded FORECLOSED at the predecessor's wrap — the endpoint demonstrably opens on a hosted runner (run 35192876641), so an exclusion could only have been ratified on a false basis. Carrying an unreachable arm in the acceptance invites a future chunk to reach for it. Arm 1 is unchanged to the character; its premise was re-verified at HEAD this phase: Assert-A11yVerdict grades the driven-session banner, the `Spec Files:` failed count and skips against an expected set of two, and NO pass tally (agent-run.ps1:62,68-100; agent-run.sh:188,193-226), which is exactly the printed verdict, counts and expected set the acceptance names.

ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED, and it is larger than the predecessor recorded. The predecessor framed the single red `:384` as a counting-basis defect in that one assertion. Measured this phase on the dev host at runtime 153 (10 passing / 2 failing / 2 skipped): `tabCycleNames()` (accessibility.e2e.ts:185) walks waiting for a BODY sentinel that this webview's Tab cycle never produces, so both 20-iteration caps exhaust and collection begins at an arbitrary position. `:397` (SC 2.4.3) fails for the SAME cause, as `Start then DIV` — its pass on runtime 131 was walk-start luck, not the wrap-insensitivity previously recorded. One defect, two reds.

The "12 visits / 6 distinct" framing is right about elements and misleading about names: the idle console has SIX focusable elements but only FIVE distinct accessible names, because CoverageMatrix.tsx:60 and RunReport.tsx:47 are unnamed `div tabIndex=0` scroll regions that both project to the string DIV. A name-keyed set basis therefore yields 5 against 6 and stays red; the repair keys on element identity.

CONFIGURATION, and the ruling that moved it. HEAD's a11y job was NOT the configuration that ran the arm: runs-on windows-2025 (ci.yml:250), an Evergreen 152+ floor (:282) and a Medium-integrity launcher in the asserting step (:431), against the measured-green windows-2022 + coherent 131/131 + High + no launcher. Operator ruled 2026-09-17 to move to the measured configuration. A first ruling of "no driver pin" was RE-TAKEN the same session against a measurement that had not been in front of it: on an unpinned windows-2022 the image is incoherent and unstably so — driver 151.0.4129.107 over runtime 131.0.2903.86 at run 35186499514 (session refused on the version check), driver 152.0.4191.77 over runtime 153.0.4234.32 at run 35185153012. The green run's coherence was produced BY the pin. Escalation 4 is therefore RATIFIED on a measured NET NARROWING: the egress count goes one to one, not one to two (the Evergreen fwlink leaves, ci.yml:313; `ci.yml`'s only other network call, :647, is loopback), and the arriving crossing is strictly narrower because its version derives from the image rather than floating always-latest. That also discharges escalation 2 — security-plan's stated float exit condition names a versioned Standalone Installer that does not exist, and pinning the driver retires the float by a route that does.

The acceptance quantifies over every keyboard/focus claim the requirement makes: "exactly one suite is named as its owner AND the claim is actually asserted in that suite". Closing those three means writing new keyboard coverage, which is outside this chunk's scope and belongs to a successor. Per verification-matrix-contract §Acceptance lifecycle a capability not provable by THIS chunk stays pooled with one notes line; concretizing the acceptance to admit a third "recorded gap" terminal alongside "owned" and "N/A by construction" would WEAKEN the stated outcome, which the never-weaken rule forbids. A SECOND measurement bears on any successor that takes this up: accessibility.e2e.ts:450 is vacuous by construction — its title names four claims (alertdialog role, focus trap, Escape resolves NoGo, focus restores) and its body is the this.skip() guard alone, 0 expect( calls over :450-455. What this chunk DOES ship toward the cap: a committed claim-to-owner enumeration beside the suites plus a checker that fails any owned row whose spec asserts nothing. The three gaps above therefore become mechanically visible instead of invisible, so the successor inherits a measured roster rather than a fresh search.
